name: HiPlan / GoalAct (Global Planning + Hierarchical Execution)
description: A 2025 family of hierarchical-planning agent frameworks that combine coarse global/milestone-level guidance with fine-grained local step hints. The task entry cites arXiv:2504.16563 = GoalAct ('Enhancing LLM-Based Agents via Global Planning and Hierarchical Execution', NCIIP 2025 Best Paper), which pairs a continuously-updated global plan with hierarchical execution over high-level skills (search, code, write). HiPlan (arXiv:2508.19076, 'Hierarchical Planning for LLM-Based Agents with Adaptive Global-Local Guidance') is the closely related sibling that adds a retrieval-augmented milestone library: complex tasks are decomposed into milestone action guides (general direction) plus step-wise hints (detailed actions), with milestones retrieved from an offline expert-demonstration library. Together they add an explicit hierarchical-decomposition dimension absent from flat decompose-then-dispatch approaches. NOTE: the entry name conflates two distinct papers; GoalAct = 2504.16563, HiPlan = 2508.19076 (the milestone-library description matches HiPlan).
decomposition_method: LLM-prompted hybrid with retrieval augmentation. GoalAct: the controller LLM produces a continuously-updated global plan and decomposes execution into high-level skills (searching, coding, writing, etc.). HiPlan: LLM-prompted milestone-action-guide generation, augmented by retrieval from an offline milestone library (RAP) — task-level and milestone-level semantically-similar exemplars are retrieved (encoded with all-mpnet-base-v2 SentenceTransformers, inner-product similarity) and adapted into step-wise hints. Milestones are extracted from expert trajectories offline using GPT-4o.
decomposition_granularity: milestone+steps. HiPlan: two units — coarse milestone action guides (general direction) and fine-grained step-wise hints (per-action). GoalAct: high-level skills as the coarse unit, with concrete actions executed under each skill.
ordering_strategy: dynamic (continuous mid-chain re-plan). GoalAct uses a continuously-updated global plan that is revised after execution feedback (ReAct-style dynamic re-planning) while preserving a clear long-term goal. HiPlan sequences milestones as the macro skeleton and adaptively generates step hints that re-align with milestone objectives as observations arrive, correcting deviations during execution.
decomposition_validation: Implicit / guidance-based rather than a formal detector. Neither framework runs an AOP-style solvability/completeness/non-redundancy detector with a reward model before dispatch. Validation is implicit: GoalAct's continuously-updated global plan checks plan feasibility against environment feedback and revises non-executable plans; HiPlan grounds milestones in retrieved successful expert demonstrations (reducing hallucinated/infeasible plans) and uses step-wise hints to detect and correct deviations during execution. No explicit pre-dispatch coverage check. [uncertain]
hierarchy_depth: two-level (milestone/skill + step). Both are explicitly hierarchical: HiPlan = milestone action guides over step-wise hints; GoalAct = high-level skills over concrete actions. This is the defining contribution vs. flat-list decomposers.
router_type: graph/hierarchical planner with retrieve-then-rerank (HiPlan). HiPlan retrieves semantically similar tasks and milestones (task-level + milestone-level retrieval) to ground the milestone plan, then adapts trajectory segments into hints. GoalAct is a global planner that maps the task onto a fixed set of high-level skills (skill selection per execution step) rather than retrieving from a large external skill pool.
routing_model: prompted LLM (same model end-to-end) plus embedding similarity for retrieval (HiPlan). HiPlan: all components — milestone guide generation, step-hint construction, final action prediction — run on the same underlying LLM (evaluated with Mixtral-8x22B-Instruct and LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct); retrieval uses embedding similarity (all-mpnet-base-v2). GoalAct: prompted LLM (GPT-4o-mini, Qwen-max, GLM-4-Plus) selects among high-level skills. No separate fine-tuned or RL router.
handles_ambiguity: best-effort with grounded guidance. Ambiguity is mitigated, not explicitly resolved via user interaction: HiPlan grounds the next action in retrieved expert milestones and step hints, biasing toward demonstrated-correct behavior; GoalAct's global plan provides macroscopic direction so the agent avoids getting stuck in local branches. Neither issues clarification requests, abstains, or uses POMDP-based disambiguation. [uncertain]
fallback_behavior: retry via re-plan / deviation correction. GoalAct continuously updates the global plan when steps prove non-executable, effectively retrying with a revised plan. HiPlan uses step-wise hints to correct deviations and re-align with milestone objectives when the agent strays. No human-escalation or hard abort node described; if no skill/milestone matches, the agent falls back to the base LLM's own action prediction. [uncertain]
skill_pool_scale_and_retrieval: embedding retrieval over a milestone library (HiPlan) vs. fixed small skill set (GoalAct). HiPlan scales by retrieving top-k semantically similar tasks/milestones from an offline-constructed library (indexed by inner-product similarity), avoiding full-context injection of all experience. GoalAct uses a small, extensible fixed set of high-level skills (search/code/write/...) selected in-context rather than a large retrieved pool — so it is full-context over a tiny skill set, not large-scale retrieval.
router_agent_asymmetry: None/low. The same LLM performs planning, retrieval-conditioned hint generation, and execution, so there is no deliberate router-vs-agent information asymmetry as formalized by SkillRouter; retrieved context is shared with the acting model. [uncertain]
execution_pattern: sequential hierarchical with ReAct-style loop. GoalAct: hierarchical execution decomposes actions into high-level skills, executed step-by-step within a continuously-updated global plan (ReAct-like observe-act-replan loop). HiPlan: follows the milestone skeleton sequentially, generating and acting on step-wise hints per milestone in a long-horizon decision loop (tasks can exceed 50 steps in ALFWorld).
parallel_vs_concurrent: Neither emphasizes parallel/concurrent tool calls; execution is a sequential long-horizon action loop guided by the hierarchy. The hierarchy reduces per-step planning complexity rather than enabling intra-turn parallelism. [uncertain]
dependency_detection: LLM-prompted / plan-implicit. Dependencies are handled implicitly through the global plan and milestone ordering (the planner determines what must precede what); there is no separate explicit DAG export or learned dependency classifier. Sequencing is conservative/sequential by default with dynamic revision. [uncertain]
result_aggregation: iterative (each result feeds the next step/plan update). Outputs of executed actions feed back into GoalAct's continuously-updated global plan and into HiPlan's step-hint generation aligning current observations to the next milestone. For long-horizon environment tasks the 'final result' is the achieved environment state / completed objective rather than a separately merged text answer.
mid_chain_feedback: hard (explicit re-planning / re-alignment). GoalAct explicitly and continuously updates the global plan from execution feedback. HiPlan dynamically adapts trajectory segments into step-wise hints that correct deviations and bridge gaps to milestone objectives — both are strong mid-chain feedback mechanisms, a key differentiator from plan-locked-upfront approaches.
benchmark_name: GoalAct: LegalAgentBench (300 tasks, 6 types, 1-hop to 5-hop legal reasoning + legal document writing). HiPlan: ALFWorld (6 household task types, sequences >50 steps) and WebShop (200 test instructions).
multi_intent_coverage: Yes, via long-horizon compound tasks (mostly sequential/dependent). LegalAgentBench multi-hop tasks and ALFWorld multi-step household tasks require dependent sub-task chains rather than independent parallel intents. Coverage is sequential/mixed; explicit independent-parallel multi-intent categories (BFCL-style) are not the focus.
accuracy_metric: outcome / state-based success rate (primary), plus task-type reward. GoalAct: success rate on LegalAgentBench (+12.22% avg over best baseline; +14.45% GPT-4o-mini, +10.09% Qwen-max, +12.11% GLM-4-Plus). HiPlan: success rate (fraction of fully-satisfied tasks) and, for WebShop, average reward (attribute alignment) — world-state/outcome-based metrics. Ablations score the contribution of milestone guides vs. step hints.
clarification_capability: None. Neither framework measures or implements when-to-ask vs. when-to-answer behavior or clarification efficiency; they pursue autonomous long-horizon execution without user clarification turns. Not evaluated on ClarifyBench/InteractComp-style metrics.
process_vs_outcome_eval: Outcome-primary with process ablation. Headline metrics are outcome/state-based success rates; the complementary value of intermediate hierarchical components (milestone action guide vs. step-wise hints; global plan vs. skill execution) is validated via ablation studies rather than a formal process-reward model.
eval_stability: Mixed. HiPlan uses well-established simulated environments (ALFWorld, WebShop) which are largely reproducible/offline, though milestone-library construction and some judging use GPT-4o (API-dependent). GoalAct's LegalAgentBench is a fixed, data-leak-resistant dataset but evaluation depends on commercial LLM controllers, so cross-paper numbers are sensitive to model/version drift. No StableToolBench-style cached API layer. [uncertain]
integration_pattern: in-context framework / standalone agent with offline retrieval index (HiPlan). Both are prompt-driven agent frameworks layered over a base LLM. HiPlan adds an offline phase that builds the milestone library (GPT-4o segmentation + SentenceTransformers embeddings + inner-product index) consulted online during execution. GoalAct is an in-context planning+execution loop. Not implemented as LangGraph nodes or inference-engine-layer routers per the papers. Code available (github.com/cjj826/GoalAct).
routing_layer: application-layer. All planning, skill/milestone selection, retrieval, and execution occur at the application/agent layer via LLM prompting and an offline retrieval index; nothing is pushed into an inference-engine or proxy layer.
latency_overhead: Moderate-to-high (amortized hierarchy). Adds planning/replanning LLM calls plus, for HiPlan, embedding-retrieval lookups and per-milestone step-hint generation. The hierarchy is intended to reduce per-step planning complexity (smaller, better-grounded decisions) at the cost of extra guidance-generation calls; HiPlan's milestone library is built offline so its online cost is retrieval + hint generation rather than re-deriving plans from scratch. [uncertain]
online_adaptation: static at deploy for the policy; experience reuse via offline library (HiPlan). Neither uses online RL/bandit updating of routing from production feedback. HiPlan does enable structured experience reuse, but the milestone library is constructed offline from expert demonstrations and is not continuously updated from live production logs in the described setup. GoalAct adapts within an episode (continuous global re-planning) but not across deployments. [uncertain]
adoption: paper-only / open-source. GoalAct: open-source code released (github.com/cjj826/GoalAct), NCIIP 2025 Best Paper. HiPlan: research paper (arXiv:2508.19076); code availability not confirmed. Both are research-grade, no commercial API/production deployment reported. [uncertain]
